quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_bonefort_beac: The Bones of the North Ribs
For Toji the beacon keeper, drive off the bone gulls pecking at the beacon, then look at the bones of the North Ribs.
The marker at the North Ribs read "Not the stone whale's bones. Older." Toji looked up at the bone wall of the fort and said nothing.
Bone gulls flock to the beacon frame and peck at the marrow. Drive off four in the hills around the fort.
Drive off bone gulls (hills around the fort)
West-northwest of the fort: the North Ribs, bones said to have fallen from the sky. See whether they match the fort's bone wall.
Look at the North Ribs (west-northwest of the fort)
The marker said "Not the stone whale's bones." Tell Toji.
The beacon faces the capital. On clear nights I light three fires to send "all is well".
...Sometimes a light shows past the eastern cape too. Who lights it, I couldn't say.
The beacon doesn't reach past the eastern cape. ...And the light out there goes dark whenever we light ours. Has done since I was young.

Since the stone whale went to sleep, the bone wall has stopped ringing. Even when the wind goes through, it is silent.
...Maybe the old bones went to sleep with it.

The bone gulls peck at the beacon frame and suck out the marrow. Drive off four or so.
And go and look at the North Ribs to the west-northwest. They say this fort's wall was built from bones hauled from there. ...They don't ring like the stone whale's.
The gulls are in the hills around the fort. The North Ribs are west-northwest. There should be a marker.
Did you see it? What did it say?
Tell him "Not the stone whale's bones. Older."

Older, eh. ...So something fell from the sky before the titans did.
And we built our wall from it and sleep inside. ...Here. Take this for your trouble.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_bonefort_scri: For Setsu the copyist, visit the Scriptorium and the Hushed Abbey.
The last page of the book at the Scriptorium was still blank. The Hushed Abbey said "Do not ring the bell." Setsu set down her brush without writing a word.
The Scriptorium west-northwest of the fort, and the Hushed Abbey west-southwest. The book of titan names Setsu was copying may still be in one of them.
Visit the Scriptorium (west-northwest of the fort)
Visit the Hushed Abbey (west-southwest of the fort)
The last page was still blank. Tell Setsu.
The titans' names change by one letter every time you copy them. So at the abbey we copied them fresh every morning.
...When a name stops changing, that titan has gone to sleep.

The last name... when you try to write it, the page turns cold. Like frost.
...I think it is the name of something in the north, somewhere colder.

This morning the stone whale's name didn't change. ...It's asleep.
Copying it feels a little lonely now.

I used to copy the names of the titans at the Scriptorium. But I could never write the last one. Every time I tried, my brush stopped.
I can't go back there now. Would you look at the Scriptorium to the west-northwest and the Hushed Abbey to the west-southwest, and see what became of the book?
The Scriptorium is west-northwest of the fort, the Hushed Abbey west-southwest. ...If there's a bell, don't ring it.
Tell her it was still blank

Still blank. ...I see. No one could write it. It wasn't only me.
This is a box I took from the abbey. I never could open it. You keep it.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_bellwatch_cro: The Nine Stones and the Backwarden Graves
For Otome the bell-listener, visit the Nine Stones and the Backwarden Graves.
The Nine Stones read "Titans: four. The other five still sleep." Her husband's name was not at the Backwarden Graves. Otome fell silent and listened for the bell.

The Nine Stones south-southeast of the hamlet and the Backwarden Graves to the east. Otome's husband climbed the stone whale's back and never came down. See whether his name is on a grave, and what the stones say.
Visit the Nine Stones (south-southeast of the hamlet)
Visit the Backwarden Graves (east of the hamlet)
The stones said "the other five still sleep", and his name was on no grave. Tell Otome.
This hamlet is the farthest the capital's great bell can reach. Only on days the wind blows from the southeast, you hear it, ever so faint.
On those days we all count how many times it rings.

Some say the other five of the Nine Stones are across the sea, up in the sky, and under the ground.
...A fisherman once said he saw an island in the north-west sea where frost comes down. Maybe that is one of the stones.

The night the stone whale went to sleep, the bell rang nine times. ...It's always eight.
Who do you suppose struck the ninth?

My husband climbed the stone whale's back and never came down. Go and see if his name is at the Backwarden Graves to the east.
And the Nine Stones to the south-southeast. The number of stones doesn't match the number of titans. ...Tell me what's written there.
The graves are east of the hamlet, the stones south-southeast. ...If you hear the bell, stop and count.
Tell her his name was not there, and the stones said "the other five still sleep"

Not there. ...Then maybe he's still on his way down.
The other five, is it. Let them not all wake while I'm alive. ...Here. This was his box.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_bellwatch_min: For Iwao the bluestone miner, drive off the rock shell beetles and look at the Bluestone Mine.
The walls of the Bluestone Mine were still wet. Iwao said, "I won't dig while the tears are wet."
Rock shell beetles roam around the hamlet, piling their shells over the mine's mouth. Drive off four.
Drive off rock shell beetles (around the hamlet)
The Bluestone Mine east-southeast of the hamlet. They say the blue stone is the stone whale's tears. See whether the walls are still wet.
Look at the Bluestone Mine (east-southeast of the hamlet)
The walls were still wet. Tell Iwao.
Polish bluestone and something seems to swim inside. The capital folk pay well and call it a jewel...
I think it's trapped.

The deepest shaft runs north-west. In my grandfather's day a cold wind came up from it and they stopped digging.
...It must run under the sea to somewhere.

The mine walls are starting to dry. ...The whale's stopped crying.
Next year I can dig. ...Somehow that feels like a loss.

The rock shell beetles have piled their shells over the mine's mouth. Can't get in. Drive off four or so.
Then go and see if the walls of the mine to the east-southeast are wet. Bluestone is the stone whale's tears. Dig while they're wet and nothing good comes of it.
The beetles are around the hamlet. The mine is east-southeast. Put a hand to the wall.
Tell him it was still wet

Still wet. ...Then no digging this year either. I'll wait till the whale stops crying.
Since I can't dig, take this instead.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_lightvillage_: For Minato the lightkeeper's apprentice, drive off the sand burrowers and visit the Northcape Light.
On the wall of the Northcape Light was the count of nights the keeper had kept: nine thousand. Minato decided to count the next one himself.
Sand burrowers lurk in the grassland between the hamlet and the cape, tripping up the oil carriers. Drive off four.
Drive off sand burrowers (grassland around the hamlet)
The Northcape Light, southeast of the hamlet. The old keeper counted one night at a time. See what the count is now.
Visit the Northcape Light (southeast of the hamlet)
The count was nine thousand. Tell Minato.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_lightvillage_app:
This hamlet is all lightkeepers' houses. North cape, east cape, south cape — everyone takes turns lighting them.
If a light ever goes out, nobody sleeps that night. We all watch the sea.

They say there used to be a light even further north than the north cape. On top of an old fort.
...No one lights it now. But sometimes it shines anyway.

Since the tide shell went to sleep, the sea's been calm. No ships come looking for the light any more.
...I still light it, though. Nine thousand and... what was it now.

The keeper at the Northcape Light counted one night at a time, every night. I'm to take over after them... but nobody knows what the count is now.
Would you go to the cape to the southeast and look? And if you could drive off four or so sand burrowers in the grassland on the way, that'd help. They trip us up when we carry the oil.
The burrowers are under the sand in the grassland. The Northcape Light is southeast. I think the count is carved on the wall.
Tell him it was nine thousand

Nine thousand... They'd been counting since before I was born.
So tonight I'm nine thousand and one. ...Thanks. This box was given to me for lamp oil. It's better off with a traveller than with me.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_lightvillage_: We Thought It Was an Island
For Ao the beachcomber, visit the Northern Strand wreck and the Tidewatch Ruin.
The wreck read "Ran aground on the tide shell's back. We thought it was an island," and the tower, "The sea bottom showed a back." Ao returned her shells to the sea.
The Northern Strand wreck east of the hamlet, and the Tidewatch Ruin to the south. Where do the huge shells Ao finds come from? Both places hold words left by people long ago.
Visit the Northern Strand wreck (east of the hamlet)
Visit the Tidewatch Ruin (south of the hamlet)
Both wrote about a "back". Tell Ao.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_lightvillage_com:
Beachcombing is all about first thing in the morning. When the tide's out, you pick up what the night sea left behind.
...Sometimes things move before you pick them up, though.

When was that morning the tower saw a back, I wonder. ...Grandma said it was off the old fort to the north.
Even now, at low tide, oddly shaped rocks show out there.

Since the tide shell went to sleep, the big shells stopped washing up.
...I feel lonely, and relieved.

The shells I find on the beach are getting bigger lately. Bigger than my hand. There's no shellfish that size in the sea.
The wreck to the east and the Tidewatch Ruin to the south — people long ago left writing at both. Would you go and look? ...I want to know where these shells come from.
The wreck is east of the hamlet, the tower south. ...If you see shells lying about, don't pick them up.
Tell her both were about the tide shell's back

A back... So these shells flaked off the tide shell.
I'll give them back. ...I feel like they weren't mine to take. This is a box I found on the beach. I don't think this one needs returning.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_tidefort_watc: For Kaji of the Tidewall watch, drive off the reef scuttlers and see how many steps of the Sunken Tower remain.
The Sunken Tower's marker said "four steps left", but only three showed above the sand. Kaji said he would build the fort's wall one course higher.
Reef scuttlers swarm the beaches and marshes around the fort, digging under the wall at night. Drive off five.
Drive off reef scuttlers (shores around the fort)
The Sunken Tower, north-northwest of the fort. It sinks one step into the sand each year. Compare the count on its marker with the steps actually left.
The marker said four, but only three showed. Tell Kaji.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_tidefort_watch.i:
The Tidewall's been built up a course every time the tide came. In my grandfather's day it was knee-high.
Now look at it. ...Is the sea rising, or the land sinking?
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_tidefort_watch.h:
Off the south coast, by the cape of hardened lava. At night the sea glows red there.
...And the Sunken Tower leans that way, too.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_tidefort_watch.a:
Since the tide shell went to sleep, the tide doesn't reach the wall. ...No need to build it up.
My hands are idle. I count scuttlers.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_tidefort_watch.q:
The reef scuttlers dig under the wall every night. Drive off five or so.
And the Sunken Tower to the north-northwest. It sinks one step a year. Its marker should say "four steps left". ...Count whether four really remain.
The scuttlers are on the beaches and marshes. The tower is north-northwest. Count the steps above the sand.
Tell him the marker said four, but only three showed

Three... It's sinking faster.
It isn't the sand that's sinking. Something underneath is going down. ...I'll raise the wall a course. Here's your pay.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_tidefort_netm: For Fusa the net mender, visit the Whaler's Wreck and the Brine Hulk.
The whaler's rudder still faced east. The Brine Hulk told of survivors whose fire went out in three days. Fusa finished mending her husband's net.
The Whaler's Wreck northwest of the fort, and the Brine Hulk to the north-northeast. Fusa's husband sailed on a ship that chased the whale in the sky. One of them may hold a trace of it.
Visit the Whaler's Wreck (northwest of the fort)
Visit the Brine Hulk (north-northeast of the fort)
The rudder faced east; the fire went out in three days. Tell Fusa.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_tidefort_netmend:
You don't mend a net starting at the tear. You start around it and draw it in, bit by bit.
...Waiting for someone's the same.

Have you heard of the sunken shrine off the east coast? On the lowest tide of the year, only its roof shows.
My husband said people once worshipped the whale there.

The night the tide shell went to sleep, a net washed up on the beach. ...Tied my husband's way.
Where do you suppose it drifted from.

My husband sailed on a ship that chased the whale in the sky. You'll laugh. But they really did chase it.
The whaler's wreck to the northwest, and the brine hulk to the north-northeast. One of them may be his ship. Go and look for me. I've promised myself not to leave this spot until I've finished mending this net.
The whaler's northwest of the fort, the brine hulk north-northeast. ...They'll both be facing the sea.
Tell her the rudder faced east and the fire lasted three days

The rudder east... He faced the whale to the very end.
Then I won't need this net. It's mended, and that's enough. ...This was his box. I'd like you to have it.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_emberfort_smi: For Tatara the fort smith, drive off the ember jackals and read the words on the Black Gate.
The Black Gate read "Fire comes from below. Return it below." Tatara let one of the forge fires die.
Ember jackals roam the badlands around the fort, hunting the charcoal carriers in packs. Drive off four.
Drive off ember jackals (badlands around the fort)
The Black Gate, west of the fort: the ash folk's gate. Read the words carved on it.
Read the Black Gate (west of the fort)
It said "Return it below." Tell Tatara.
The fort's wall is earth baked hard in the forge. A wall fired in flame stands up to flame.
...So I thought. The ember jackals come and lick the wall to warm themselves.

On the shore to the east-southeast, a tube of hardened lava gapes open. It is still hot inside.
...Maybe the "below" on the Black Gate means a place like that.

Since the Ember went to sleep, the borrowed fire has calmed a little.
...I'll give it back bit by bit, before I'm told to.

Ember jackals are running the charcoal carriers ragged. No charcoal, and the forge goes cold. Drive off four.
Then the Black Gate to the west. The ash folk carved something on it. ...My forge fire was borrowed from a crack in the ground. If it says to give it back, I'll have to.
The jackals are in the badlands around the fort. The Black Gate is west. Look at the pillars.
Tell him "Fire comes from below. Return it below."

Return it below, eh. ...Right. I've been borrowing it all this time.
I'll let one forge go out. The rest are enough to work with. ...Take this in place of wages.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_emberfort_sur: The Watch Who Watched the Sky
For Shino, a survivor of Ashwatch Fort, clear the cinder mites and look at the fort's watchtower.
Ashwatch Fort's marker read "The watch looked to the sky to the end. The fire came from below." Shino began watching the ground instead of the sky.
Cinder mites swarm on the way to Ashwatch Fort, nesting in the ash. Drive off five.
Drive off cinder mites (badlands around the fort)
Ashwatch Fort, to the west, where Shino once kept watch. See what remains on its watchtower.
Look at Ashwatch Fort's watchtower (west of the fort)
It said "The fire came from below." Tell Shino.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_emberfort_surviv:
Keeping watch — the days when nothing comes are far longer. You watch an empty sky for ever.
...I don't remember much about the day it came.

Watching the ground, sometimes there are warm patches. The further east, the warmer.
...I think there's fire over there that hasn't come up yet.

The Ember is asleep. ...Sky and ground both quiet.
I never knew having nothing to watch could be so unsettling.

I was a watch at Ashwatch Fort. That night too, I was watching the sky. I thought if the Ember came, it'd come from the sky.
Go west to Ashwatch Fort and see what's left on the watchtower. And clear about five cinder mites on the way. They breed in the ash and I can't get near.
The mites are where the ash piles up. Ashwatch is to the west.
Tell her it said "The fire came from below"

From below. ...Yes. We were all looking at the sky.
From now on I'll watch the ground. That's the watch left to me. ...This is a box I carried out of the fort. I'll leave it with you.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_smokewatch_re: The Forge of the Cracked Bell
For Yu the smoke reader, drive off the ash draggers and visit the Northern Forge.
The Northern Forge was where the capital's bell was cast; the cracked bell was brought back there. Yu said now he understood why the smoke always drifts toward the capital.
Ash draggers roam around the hamlet, tangling the lines of smoke. Drive off three.
Drive off ash draggers (around the hamlet)
The Northern Forge, west of the hamlet. Its smoke alone drifts toward the capital, against the wind. Find out what it forged.
Visit the Northern Forge (west of the hamlet)
It was where the capital's bell was cast. Tell Yu.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_smokewatch_reade:
In Smokewatch we send up smoke first thing and decide the day by how it bends.
Straight up, we go out. Bends north, we stay in. ...The days it bends south, no one speaks.

Down on the south-east shore there's a spot where smoke comes straight out of the ground. No one lit it.
...I tried to read it. The letters are upside down.

The morning the Ember went to sleep, the smoke went straight up. ...First time in decades.
Today's a day for going out. Where to, the smoke won't say.

Smoke drifts with the wind. Obviously. But the smoke from the Northern Forge to the west drifts toward the capital, against the wind.
Go and see what that forge made. And drive off three or so ash draggers. When they pass, the smoke lines tangle and I can't read them.
The draggers are around the hamlet. The Northern Forge is west. Read the marker.
Tell him it cast the capital's bell, and the cracked bell was returned there

The capital's bell... The cracked bell went home to the forge it was born in.
Then that smoke is calling to the bell. Toward the new one: "Over here." ...Here, for your trouble.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_smokewatch_tw: For Yoru the twin, visit the Twins' House and the Drip Cave.
On the pillar of the Twins' House, one height mark stopped partway. The Drip Cave said "Fell asleep at nine hundred." Yoru added one small mark above the one that stopped.
The Twins' House northwest of the hamlet, and the Drip Cave west-northwest. Yoru's twin loved to count the drops falling in the cave.
Visit the Twins' House (northwest of the hamlet)
Visit the Drip Cave (west-northwest of the hamlet)
One mark stopped; the cave said "fell asleep at nine hundred." Tell Yoru.
They say when one twin runs a fever, the other gets sick too.
...The night they were gone, I was freezing. Even with the Ember's fire right on top of us.

They come to me in dreams. On a white island in the north, counting the sound of water. They try to count past nine hundred and fall asleep again.
...Is there an island like that up north?

The night the Ember went to sleep, I counted to nine hundred too. ...Couldn't sleep.
Maybe their turn isn't over yet.

I had a twin. At our house to the northwest, we marked our heights on the pillar. ...Their marks stop partway.
Go to the Drip Cave to the west-northwest too. They loved counting the drops there. See if anything's left.
The house is northwest of the hamlet, the cave west-northwest. ...Listen closely inside the cave.
Tell him one mark stopped, and the cave said "fell asleep at nine hundred"

Nine hundred... They always fell asleep counting to nine hundred. Right to the end.
I'll add a little mark above the one that stopped. ...This is a box they found. Open it for them.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_frostfort_hun: For Shimo the Frostwall hunter, drive off the static puffs and look at the Thunderstone Ring.
The Thunderstone Ring read "The ninth seat is still empty." Shimo decided that even if he found a lightning-struck stone, he would leave it be.
Static puffs drift around the fort, clinging to the wall's copper nails. Drive off five.
Drive off static puffs (around the fort)
The Thunderstone Ring, south-southwest of the fort, where only lightning-struck stones are set. See how many are there.
Visit the Thunderstone Ring (south-southwest of the fort)
The ninth seat was empty. Tell Shimo.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_frostfort_hunter:
They call it Frostwall because the wall freezes into a wall of frost in winter. When the thunder wing comes, frost doesn't burn.
...It melts, mind.

In the sea west-northwest there's a little island where frost falls. Its shore is white even in summer.
I once tracked game as far as the ferry over there. The ferryman told me: "Crossing's fine. As long as you mean to come back."

Since the thunder wing went to sleep, there are fewer puffs. The nails are quiet.
...So quiet it keeps me awake.

The static puffs cling to the wall's copper nails, crackling all night. Can't sleep. Drive off five or so.
And the Thunderstone Ring to the south-southwest. A ring of lightning-struck stones. My father said "when there are nine, something comes." See how many are set now.
The puffs float around the fort. The Thunderstone Ring is south-southwest.
Tell him the ninth seat was empty

Still eight. ...Can I call that good?
I'd meant to haul one over if I found a struck stone. Maybe I won't. ...Here, your due.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_frostfort_fle: A Feather Taller Than a Man
For Haya the fletcher, visit the Brokenwing Tower and the Cloudwatch Post.

A feather taller than a man was stuck in the Brokenwing Tower. The Cloudwatch Post read "On days the clouds flow east, the thunder wing sleeps in the west." Haya decided never to make arrows from that feather.

The Brokenwing Tower and the Cloudwatch Post, both south of the fort. A huge feather is said to be stuck in the tower — see if it could fletch arrows. The post may tell how to read where the feather's owner is.
Visit the Brokenwing Tower (south of the fort)
Visit the Cloudwatch Post (south of the fort)
The feather was taller than a man. Tell Haya.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_frostfort_fletch:
Frostwall arrows are fletched on frosty mornings. The cold shrinks the feather so it grips tight.
...Shrinks your fingers too.

Once, at the landing for the western islet, I picked up a feather. Pure white, so cold my fingers nearly froze.
...Not a thunder wing feather. I don't know whose it was.

Since the thunder wing went to sleep, it doesn't matter which way the clouds flow.
No one reads the post's words now. ...I still do.

Not just any feather will fletch an arrow. Feathers that have been struck by lightning fly true.
I heard an enormous feather is stuck in the Brokenwing Tower to the south. Would you go and look? And the Cloudwatch Post too. It might tell where the feather's owner is.
The tower and the post are both south of the fort. ...Don't touch the feather.
Tell her the feather was taller than a man, and when clouds flow east the thunder wing sleeps in the west

Taller than a man... That's a thunder wing feather. It didn't moult. It hit the tower and snapped.
I can't make arrows from that. Shoot one and it'll fly home to its owner. ...Take this instead.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_windmill_keep: For Kazami the windmill keeper, drive off the peak fledglings and visit the Kitemaker's House.
The Kitemaker's House said "Kite string is twisted from copper, to send the lightning into the ground." Kazami wound copper string around the windmill's axle.
Peak fledglings come down around the hamlet and peck holes in the windmill sails. Drive off four.
Drive off peak fledglings (around the hamlet)
The Kitemaker's House, northeast of the hamlet. They flew kites even in thunderstorms. Find out how they kept the lightning off.
Visit the Kitemaker's House (northeast of the hamlet)
The kite string was copper. Tell Kazami.
They say the best flour in Windmill comes from grinding on thunder nights.
...We grind it at risk of our lives. It had better be good.

Past the northern mountains, in the sea, there's a frost isle. The wind from there doesn't smell of thunder.
...Maybe it's so cold even lightning freezes.

Since the thunder wing went to sleep, no thunder nights. The flour tastes a bit worse.
...Listen to me complain.

On thunder nights the lightning hits the windmill. Scorched sails, split axle. Rebuilt it twice last year.
They say the kitemakers to the northeast flew kites even in thunderstorms without a care. Go and see how. And four peak fledglings — they come to peck the sails.
The fledglings come down around the hamlet. The Kitemaker's House is northeast.
Tell him the string was twisted copper, sending the lightning into the ground

Copper string, into the ground... I see. You don't stop the lightning — you give it a way through.
I'll wind copper round the axle. No third rebuild this year. ...Your thanks.
quest.skyabyss.town.hamlet_windmill_moss: For Midori the moss keeper, visit the South Moss Shrine and the Rumble Cave.
The moss at the South Moss Shrine glowed blue with drunk lightning. Deep in the Rumble Cave, thunder rolled under a clear sky. Midori drew the path the thunder takes from the cave to the shrine.
The South Moss Shrine north of the hamlet, and the Rumble Cave north-northeast. The shrine's moss is said to drink lightning. Compare the two and see where the cave's thunder comes from.
Visit the South Moss Shrine (north of the hamlet)
Visit the Rumble Cave (north-northeast of the hamlet)
The moss glowed; the cave rumbled. Tell Midori.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_windmill_mossgua:
Moss turns blue when it drinks lightning. Too much and it goes white and dies.
So on thunder nights we share it out a little at a time. Moss and people both have their proper share.

The thunder deep in the cave seems to come from the north. Further north, from the sea where the snow falls.
...Is thunder born somewhere cold, I wonder.

Since the thunder wing went to sleep, the moss will not turn blue. ...It is slowly going white.
Without thunder, even moss goes hungry.

I keep the moss at the shrine to the north. It drinks lightning — on thunder nights everyone sees the night out at the shrine.
But lately the moss glows even on clear days. And they say thunder rolls inside the Rumble Cave to the north-northeast, clear sky or not. ...I think they're connected. Would you look at both?
The shrine is north of the hamlet, the cave north-northeast. ...If your hair stands on end in the cave, get out at once.
Tell her the moss glowed and the cave rumbled under a clear sky

I knew it. The cave's thunder runs under the ground to the shrine, and the moss drinks it.
I'll draw the path. Then we'll know where to sit at the shrine on thunder nights. ...This is a box from the shrine's offerings. From the moss keeper to a traveller.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_isle_ferryman.as:
Crossing over? This strait numbs your fingers even in summer.
Climb in.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_isle_ferryman.se:
Frost Isle was not always an island, they say. Ice joined it to the mainland and you could walk across.
...No one goes into the interior. The frost is too deep. Those who do mostly do not come back.
quest.skyabyss.town.whale_bone.title: The Singing Ribs
quest.skyabyss.town.whale_bone.summary: For Gonji the bone carver, drive off the moss crawlers that gnaw at the bone yard, then hear whether the Singing Ribs still sing.
quest.skyabyss.town.whale_bone.done: The Singing Ribs hummed low each time the wind went through. Gonji says he picks which bone to carve by that sound.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_whale_bonecarver:
Moss crawlers have been swarming the bones in the yard lately. They gnaw right through, moss and all. Would you drive off three or so?
And while you are out, go north-northeast to the Singing Ribs and hear whether they still sing. ...I choose which bone to carve by that sound.
The crawlers are in the grass and woods outside town. The Singing Ribs are north-northeast. ...Listen closely.

Low, was it. ...Good. Then they can still be carved. A bone that has stopped singing splits when you carve it.
Take this whetstone for your trouble. I use it on bone, but it works on a blade just as well.
quest.skyabyss.town.whale_bone.kill.jour: Moss crawlers roam the grass and woods outside town. They gnaw the bones, moss and all. Drive off about three.
quest.skyabyss.town.whale_bone.kill.kill: Drive off moss crawlers (grass and woods outside town)
quest.skyabyss.town.whale_bone.go.journa: North-northeast of town: the Singing Ribs. They say the bones sing when the wind goes through. Go and hear whether they still do.
quest.skyabyss.town.whale_bone.go.go: Hear the Singing Ribs (north-northeast of town)
quest.skyabyss.town.whale_bone.back.jour: The ribs hummed low. Tell Gonji.
quest.skyabyss.town.whale_watch.title: The Bell of the Whalewatch Post
quest.skyabyss.town.whale_watch.summary: For Haru the bell-ringer, go to the Whalewatch Post to the east and see which way the stone whale is heading.
quest.skyabyss.town.whale_watch.done: The board at the Whalewatch Post read "If the stone whale turns over in its sleep, strike the bell three times." Haru has counted the strokes ever since.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_whale_lookout.q_:
I'm the town's bell-ringer. When the stone whale shows, I ring the bell. But nobody remembers how many times.
They say the old watch's rule is written at the Whalewatch Post to the east. Would you go and see? And which way the whale is facing, too.
The Whalewatch Post is east of town. From the top you can see the whole sky.
Well? How many times did it say?
Tell him "three times if it turns over"

Three... only three when it turns over. So the rest of the time, once is enough.
Thanks! These are the watch's snacks. ...And tell Isana I found it out myself, okay?
quest.skyabyss.town.whale_watch.go.journ: East of town: the Whalewatch Post, where the old watch kept their eyes on the sky. Look at which way the stone whale is heading, and read the board.
quest.skyabyss.town.whale_watch.go.go: Watch the whale from the Whalewatch Post (east of town)
quest.skyabyss.town.whale_watch.back.jou: The board said "strike the bell three times". Tell Haru.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_whale_bonecarver:
A stone whale's rib keeps singing a hundred years after it falls. While it sings, it's living bone. It won't split under the knife.
...The clapper in the town bell? My grandfather carved it from a rib.

Climbing the back, are you. ...Then remember this. Whale bone rings low when struck from above, high when struck from the side.
If you lose your way up there, tap the ground under you. The low side is the core of the bone.

Since the stone whale went to sleep, the ribs in the yard sound a little softer.
...Seems even bones can hear someone breathing in their sleep.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_whale_lookout.id:
I ring the town bell. When the stone whale shows, I ring it.
Isana watches the sky from the tower all day long. Someday I want to see that far too.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_whale_lookout.hi:
You're climbing the stone whale's back? Amazing!
When the whale turns, the tail moves first. When you see the tail move, find something to hold on to. ...That's what Isana said.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_whale_lookout.af:
Since the stone whale fell asleep, there's been nothing to ring the bell for.
But every morning I ring it once. One for good morning. ...I hope it hears.
Want to cross to the capital? ...Not yet. Walk the island road first.
The bandits at the pass, the footprints in the hollow, the fire at the rest stop, then the mistletoe shrine. Come back once you've prayed there.

Those who've only just woken usually can't even remember their own name. It comes back, bit by bit, as they walk the island road.
...Some things don't come back.

You smell of the shrine. ...So you've walked the island road.
Get in. I'll row you to the Bell Capital.
quest.skyabyss.town.tide_ferry.title: The Drifted Boat
quest.skyabyss.town.tide_ferry.summary: For the ferryman, go and look at the wreck washed up on the beach.
quest.skyabyss.town.tide_ferry.done: The wreck was empty. The ferryman called it a "return boat".
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_tide_ferryman.q_:
A wreck has washed up on the east beach. ...Strange thing. I never rowed that boat, but my ferry mark is on its bow.
Would you go and look? Just tell me whether anyone was aboard.
The wreck's east of the harbour, past the beach. ...Just whether anyone was aboard.
Tell him no one was there

No one, eh. ...I see. Then it was a return boat. It carried someone to the island and came back empty.
Here, for your trouble. Some grilled fish.
quest.skyabyss.town.tide_ferry.go.journa: East of the harbour, past the beach: a wreck with the ferryman's mark on it, though he never rowed it. See if anyone was aboard.
quest.skyabyss.town.tide_ferry.go.go: Look at the beached wreck (east of the harbour)
quest.skyabyss.town.tide_ferry.back.jour: No one was there. Tell the ferryman.
quest.skyabyss.town.tide_light.title: The Old Lighthouse on the Cape
quest.skyabyss.town.tide_light.summary: For the lightkeeper, look at the old lighthouse on the cape and bring two candles.
quest.skyabyss.town.tide_light.done: The old lighthouse wall had the same carving. The lightkeeper set the candles in the window.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_tide_lightkeeper:
They say the old lighthouse on the cape has the same carving as ours. "The tide can be read. Wait."
Would you go and see? And bring two candles from the tool shop. ...I want to light one for the old one too.
Candles at the tool shop. The old lighthouse is on the cape southwest of the harbour.
Tell him the carving was there and hand over the candles

It was there. ...Same hand. The keeper before me, or the one before that.
One candle in each window: one for here, one for there. Take this. You will want it in the dark.
quest.skyabyss.town.tide_light.get.journ: Two candles. The tool shop sells them.
quest.skyabyss.town.tide_light.go.journa: An old lighthouse stands on the cape southwest of the harbour. See if the carving "The tide can be read. Wait." is on its wall.
quest.skyabyss.town.tide_light.go.go: Look at the old lighthouse (southwest of the harbour)
quest.skyabyss.town.tide_light.back.jour: The carving was there. Give the lightkeeper the candles.
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_rods.title: Copper for the Rod Tower
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_rods.summary: For the elder, look at the old lightning-rod tower and bring a copper ingot.
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_rods.done: The rod tower's copper was missing a joint that sends lightning into the ground. The elder offered the copper at the wind folk's shrine.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_storm_elder.q_as:
Would you look at the old rod tower to the southeast? Our forebears sent the lightning into the ground with it.
Lately, at squall-time, light jumps on top of it. Perhaps some copper is missing.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_storm_elder.q_wa: The tower is southeast of the village. Copper is in the village shop.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_storm_elder.q_ba: Tell him a joint was missing and hand over the copper
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_storm_elder.q_do:
A joint. ...So the lightning couldn't reach the ground and wandered on top of the tower.
I'll offer the copper at the wind folk's shrine and have the young ones mend it. For you: a wind shard. It fits a socket in your gear.
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_rods.go.journa: Southeast of the village stands an old lightning-rod tower. See how much of its copper is left.
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_rods.go.go: Look at the rod tower ruin (southeast of the village)
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_rods.get.journ: A joint is missing. One copper ingot, from the village shop.
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_hut.title: Footprints at the Wind Gate
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_hut.summary: For the hut keeper, look at the wind gate ruin and bring three loaves of bread.
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_hut.done: At the wind gate there were only footprints going up toward the peaks. The hut keeper put the bread on the shelf.
Last night a traveller went up to the peaks. I told them to come down before the thunder.
Would you check the wind gate ruin to the south, whether any footprints come back? And bring three loaves. The hut's shelf is bare.
Bread at the tool shop. The wind gate ruin is south of the village.
Tell him the footprints only went up, and hand over the bread

Only going up, eh. ...I see.
I'll put the bread on the shelf. If anyone does come down, they'll be hungry.
Take these. Up on the peaks, something harder than bread keeps better.
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_hut.get.journa: Three loaves of bread from the tool shop, for whoever stays at the hut.
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_hut.get.get: Get three loaves of bread (food vendor)
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_hut.go.journal: The wind gate ruin, south of the village. A traveller went up to the peaks at night. See if any footprints come back.
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_hut.go.go: Look at the wind gate ruin (south of the village)
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_hut.back.journ: Only footprints going up. Give the hut keeper the bread.
quest.skyabyss.town.storm_hut.back.back: Give the hut keeper the bread
quest.skyabyss.town.ember_forge.title: The Fire at the Old Forge
quest.skyabyss.town.ember_forge.summary: For the last of the ash folk, look at the old forge to the west.
quest.skyabyss.town.ember_forge.done: The ash at the old forge to the west was still warm. The last of the ash folk called it "the fire we keep".
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ember_survivor.q:
Would you look at the old forge to the west? It is where the ash folk last kept their fire.
Whether the ash is still warm. ...I cannot go near it any more.
The old forge is west of the village. Put a hand to the ash.
Tell them it was still warm

Still warm. ...So the fire we never gave back is still there.
Take this, an ash shard. A tiny piece of the fire we keep.
quest.skyabyss.town.ember_forge.go.journ: The old forge west of the village. Put a hand to the ash and see whether it is still warm.
quest.skyabyss.town.ember_forge.go.go: Look at the old forge (west of the village)
quest.skyabyss.town.ember_forge.back.jou: The ash was still warm. Tell the survivor.
quest.skyabyss.town.ember_forge.back.bac: Tell the last of the ash folk
quest.skyabyss.town.ember_watch.title: Rounds at the Burnt Fort
quest.skyabyss.town.ember_watch.summary: For the burnt fort watch, drive off three bandits and walk the burnt fort to the southwest.
quest.skyabyss.town.ember_watch.done: You drove off the bandits and walked the burnt fort. From its watchtower you could see the middle of the ember circle.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ember_watch.q_as:
Keeping watch alone wears a man down. Lend me a hand.
Drive off three of the bandits camped to the northeast, then walk the burnt fort to the southwest. Tell me how the southern sky looks from its watchtower.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ember_watch.q_wa: The camp is northeast of the village, the burnt fort southwest.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ember_watch.q_ba: Tell him the southern sky was red
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ember_watch.q_do:
Red, was it. ...From up there you can see it breathing, can't you.
Thanks. These are the watch's emergency rations. Take them.
quest.skyabyss.town.ember_watch.kill.jou: Bandits camp northeast of the village. Drive off three of them.
quest.skyabyss.town.ember_watch.go.journ: The burnt fort southwest of the village. Look at the southern sky from its watchtower.
quest.skyabyss.town.ember_watch.go.go: Walk the burnt fort (southwest of the village)
quest.skyabyss.town.ember_watch.back.bac: Report to the burnt fort watch
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_tide_ferryman.id: The capital shore and this harbour. The boat goes as often as you like. ...Don't ask who rows it.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_tide_ferryman.hi:
The tide shell? On an ebb-tide evening an island drifts in off the beach. That's its back.
You can buy a boat at the tool shop. If you row out from the beach, do it on a day the tide's out.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_tide_ferryman.af: Lately the island doesn't come in. ...Asleep, maybe. The tide still comes and goes all the same.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_tide_lightkeeper: The lighthouse fire isn't for the island. It's for whoever comes back from it. ...Few have.

There's an old carving on the lighthouse wall. 'The tide can be read. Wait.' It was there before me.
Who carved it... Funny, it looks a bit like your hand. Probably nothing.
I put out one lamp tonight. ...Felt like I needn't wait up for anyone coming back.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_storm_elder.idle: Kazamachi isn't a village that waits for wind. It waits for the wind to pass. ...Always has.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_storm_elder.hint:
The thunder wing comes down to the peaks at squall-time. Our forebears, the wind folk, sent its lightning into the ground with copper pillars.
Copper and diamonds are in the village shop. Have you seen the mirror at the old gate? ...My grandmother said a traveller once stood before it.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_storm_elder.afte: The sky over the peaks is quiet. ...Some old ones say there hasn't been an evening like this since the wind folk.
Anyone may use the hut. Just split as much firewood as you burn, for the next one.

If you climb the high peaks, come down before the thunder. There are old lightning-rod towers partway up.
Under those, the lightning doesn't strike. ...Hasn't, I should say. So far.
Lately the peaks don't thunder. Folk staying in the hut can finally sleep.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ember_survivor.i: The ash folk don't light fires. We keep them. ...And we still haven't given this one back.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ember_survivor.h:
Deep in the ember grounds there's an old forge. A single page was left there. 'Four returned, then down. This time for sure.'
The village apothecary has fire-resistance draughts. If you're walking into the fire, take two.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ember_survivor.a: The forge has gone cold. ...Maybe the fire the ash folk kept has finally gone home.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ember_watch.idle: Watch of a burnt fort, with nothing left to watch. ...At night the southern sky turns red. I watch that.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ember_watch.hint:
From the southern rise, only the middle of the ember circle glows red at night. Not fire. Breath.
Bandits and ash beasts roam. Before you leave, set your waking place at this village's inn.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ember_watch.afte: The southern sky doesn't turn red any more. ...Guess the watch will count stars from tomorrow.
dialogue.skyabyss.attendant_drunkard.men: Ask him to open the wall
dialogue.skyabyss.attendant_drunkard.tow: Hic... friend, I'm parched. Something sweet. A honey pot. Then I'll tell you my best story.
Ahh, sweet. ...Here's my best one. Under the sky there's another sky. Down at the bottom of the earth. Where the four heartbeats go home, someday.
My old man used to say the sky down there looks up at this one from below. ...Hic. Just a drunk's babble. Forget it.
Hey, d'you hear it? ...No? Go put your ear to the far wall down here.
You heard it. That's wind. Wind being sucked down, from above to below, into the deep.
There's a passage behind it. Whoever built the tavern bricked it up. ...I've got the key. But it's too early. Not till you've given back more heartbeats.
...You came. You smell of ash. You've given back three. It's time for the key.
You saw the door. ...Beyond it is the road to the sky below. Give back the fourth, and the key will point down. Come see me then.
Me? I'm not going. I knew one who went and came back. ...He'd forgotten his own name.
(The drunkard slides an old key into a seam in the wall, and two stones fall away inward.) ...Go on. There's a door at the end. Don't try to open it. Just look.
Will you hear a request? Every morning someone leaves a flower on the nameless grave. I've never once seen who.
Pick me a flower. I'd like to lay it beside mine. Whoever they are, it's lonely to mourn alone.
...Thank you. This morning's flower was this very colour. Same field, same flower.
Did you come by early this morning? ...I see. You didn't.
I found letters on the nameless grave's stone, under the moss. My eyes can't make them out. Would you fetch a bucket of water? We'll wash it.
Let's see... there. Not a name. Just one line.
"Write it down before you forget." ...Who was it meant for, I wonder. The one under the stone, or the one standing before it?
Last night someone started digging up the nameless grave. The earth is fresh. The footprints lead into the capital, toward the house of mourning on the south road.
The prints were about... the size of your boots. Would you go and look? I'd rather not go near that house.
Earth on the empty chair. A line traced in the ash on the table... "Back again."
...That grave was there before I became keeper. No one knows who dug it. I have a feeling the rest will come clear further on.
This may be my last request. I'd like to light a candle before the nameless grave. Would you bring me one?
It's lit. ...The truth is, yesterday I looked beneath the grave. The coffin was empty. It's been empty all along.
This grave was dug by someone who meant to lie in it "one day". With no name carved. For someone whose name isn't settled yet.
When you've gone further and come back, we'll talk again. Perhaps by then the letters will be readable.
You're with the apprentice? The test has two parts: drive off four night beasts, and bring back three bones. That's all a back demands.
The old pages of the roll? ...Yes, there's one line without a name. The ink is dry, but there are no letters.
dialogue.skyabyss.attendant_innkeeper.me: Leave the rumoured request for now
dialogue.skyabyss.attendant_innkeeper.to: Thank you. I'll let them know you're coming.
Oh, this child! Her family's been searching all night. ...Come here, there's warm milk. You'll sleep in one of our beds tonight.
She was in the house of mourning? ...That family's girl vanished on a thunder night three years ago. About this one's age.
That's fine. Come and hear the rumours again whenever you like.
The rest? My grandmother used to sing it. "Each time it rings, one does not return." ...Not a song for bedtime.
dialogue.skyabyss.attendant_perch_keeper: The sea song? I heard it on the beach as a child. "At the road's end, a shell rings." That's all I remember.
dialogue.skyabyss.attendant_smith.town_f: The boy built a forge? ...Hmph. Not bad. He laid the magma well. Who taught him that, I wonder.
They say a blade forged in that ash keeps a red line even when it cools. ...Don't tell the boy. It'll go to his head.
dialogue.skyabyss.attendant_storage_keep: Folk from the shore leave many parcels here they never collect. ...I know the song. "Those who do not return count in the tide's deep."
dialogue.skyabyss.attendant_tool_merchan: Lay out the fisher's catch? On tide market days I'll lend him half my shopfront. ...With all the tide shell talk, fish will sell dear.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_apprentice.hand_: How did it go? Have you got three bones?
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_apprentice.idle: I can tie these knots with my eyes shut now.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_apprentice.meet: Oh... are you a whale chaser too? I'm only an apprentice. I'm scared to sit the Whale Chasers' Guild's test alone.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_apprentice.meet2: Will you sit it with me? Ask the clerk at the desk what the test is. Everyone who rides a titan's back passed it, they say. The traveller who came before, too, I bet.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_apprentice.passe: We did it...! We'll both be on the roll now. The clerk said there's a line on an old page with no name written in it.
Maybe someone left before they could write it. ...Here, my father's iron. Still too heavy for me. You use it.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_apprentice.wait_: The clerk's at the Whale Chasers' Guild on the east avenue. I'll practise my knots here.
Four night beasts. Three bones. ...It'd help if you went first. I'll stay behind and keep count.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ash_apprentice.b: I lit the forge. The ash melted. ...And in the fire I saw a thread of light. Running down and down. Below the forge floor, further down.
The master says to forget I saw it. But I'm telling you. I think it's a road home, to somewhere.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ash_apprentice.h: Got the blast furnace and the magma?
Hand over the blast furnace and magma
Now I can build it! I'll go show the master... no, you tell him. If I say it, he'll yell that I'm not ready.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ash_apprentice.i: The ash is warm. In my hand it almost seems to pulse, slowly.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ash_apprentice.m: You're headed for the ember mountain, right? I'm apprenticed at the smithy. I bagged ash from the mountain and hauled it here. This ash never cools.
The master's forge won't melt this ash. We need a new one. One blast furnace, and four magma blocks for the bed. ...Can you get them?
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_ash_apprentice.w: The tool shop should stock both the blast furnace and magma blocks. Hairo's shop never runs out.
The master's behind the smithy counter.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_baker.hand_ask.g: Hand over the wheat sheaves and charcoal
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_baker.handed: There, it's awake. ...Done: ash-baked bread. Take it. It should stay a little warm on the road.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_baker.idle: When fresh bread is in the air, everyone goes a little quiet.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_baker.meet: Since the ash started falling, the oven won't behave. I add wood and it soon goes still, as if asleep.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_baker.meet2: Coal might keep it awake. And I'm short of wheat sheaves. Could you bring sixteen wheat sheaves and four charcoal?
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_baker.wait: Coal is the black specks in cave walls. Wheat sheaves, from the fields outside. ...I feel something pulsing slowly at the back of the oven.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_bard.back: Let me hear them. ..."At the road's end, a shell rings." "Each time it rings, one does not return." "Those who do not return count in the tide's deep."
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_bard.back2: Ah, it continues. It continued. ...So this was a song of the sea counting people. Take this as thanks. An old disc of mine, with a song from somewhere far away.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_bard.idle: ♪ When the tide draws back, a road appears...
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_bard.meet: Well met, traveller. I gather songs as I walk. I have a sea song, but it breaks off. "When the tide draws back, a road appears"... and nothing after.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_bard.meet2: Someone in the capital may remember the rest. The perch keeper, the innkeeper, the storage keeper. Would you ask the three of them for me?
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_bard.wait_listen: Bring me their words just as they say them. A song only grows in other people's mouths.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_bellkeeper.back: I heard it. ...You rang it only once?
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_bellkeeper.back2: There was a second toll. Late, and from the same height. Too clear for an echo.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_bellkeeper.back3: No, just an old man's ears. Thank you. From today the town can count its days again.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_bellkeeper.idle: May the bell ring at the same pitch today, too.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_bellkeeper.meet: Ah, young one. I'm the bell keeper. ...Was, I should say. My knees won't allow the tower stairs any more.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_bellkeeper.meet2: The top bell hasn't rung since the night the shadow passed. A bell counts the days. A town that stops counting forgets which day it is.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_bellkeeper.wait_: The tower stands on the north terrace. Ring it once, then come straight down.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_bellkeeper.why: The one below calls people. The one on top speaks to the sky. ...Once is enough. Ring it once, then come straight down.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_child.at_inn: It's warm here. ...I should have brought her too.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_child.find2: Nobody uses this bed. I thought the thunder wouldn't find me here.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_child.find3: ...But at night there's someone else in this room. A kid my size. She never talks.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_child.find3.go: Let's go to the inn. There are lights there
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_fisher.back: The merchant gave us a spot! ...The night before I ran, something like a pearl caught in my net. When I looked in, it seemed to look back. I threw it into the sea.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_fisher.back2: You're the one heading out to sea, I reckon. Take a rod instead of a net. When I can go back to the shore, let's meet again.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_fisher.hand_ask: Got the string and the cod?
Hand over the string and cod
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_fisher.handed: Bless you. Now I can cast again. I'd like to borrow the tool merchant's shopfront for the market, but I'm no talker. Would you ask for me?
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_fisher.idle: The smell of the tide is still on my fingers.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_fisher.meet: You from the capital? I fished the east shore. ...Used to. The night the tide shell came, the sea pulled back all at once. I dropped my net and ran.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_fisher.meet2: When the tide returns, there's a market. The tide market. Put fish on a stall there and I could eat again. But look at this net. Eight threads and three cod. Can you manage?
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_fisher.wait_gath: String from spiders, cod from river or sea. ...If the sea scares you, the river's fine.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_fisher.wait_mark: The tool shop's on the east corner of the square.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_herbalist.handed: A good colour. ...This will see a feverish child through the night. I'll tell them who brewed it.
One thing. Never put the ember mountain's ash into a potion. You fall, down and down, in your dreams. No one has come back yet.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_herbalist.idle: Herbs remember the weather they were picked in.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_herbalist.meet: My, you smell of ash, child. These old arms can't stir a pot any more. Show me a potion someone has brewed.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_herbalist.meet2: Pick out two potions at the apothecary for me. Any colour. ...The days of brewing your own are over, I suppose.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_herbalist.wait: The apothecary has all sorts on the shelf, doesn't it? Two, mind.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_mother.handed: Thank you. ...Look, nobody's at the window now. I baked this. The youngest wanted you to have it.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_mother.idle: Children see what grown-ups don't look at.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_mother.meet: When the thunder comes, my children count at the window. From the flash to the sound. ...The youngest says she hears wings.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_mother.meet2: Candles blow out in the wind. Could you find me three lanterns at the tool shop? One for each room.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_mother.wait: Eight iron nuggets around a torch. ...The children talk about nobody but you.
Hand over the wayfinder and map
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_sailor.handed: North. ...Good. It fills, it ebbs, it fills again. The island always comes in on the evening of an ebb. Take this; it sees far.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_sailor.idle: The smell of the tide never leaves you, even on land.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_sailor.meet: That night the tide came up to my feet. The island drew close. When I looked, the compass at my belt was gone.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_sailor.meet2: Could you get me a new one? And a blank chart. The tool shop should have both. I want to write down the ebb days before I die.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_sailor.wait: The tool shop should have both a wayfinder and a blank chart. ...I'd like to get the ebb days written down soon.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_weaver.hand_ask: Have you got the copper and the rod?
Hand over the copper and the rod
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_weaver.handed: That'll do. ...Cloth woven on thunder nights sometimes grows a pattern by itself. A wing. A bird I've never seen, and yet it feels familiar.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_weaver.handed2: Take this spyglass as thanks. My father used it on the peaks. From somewhere high, you can see the sky's shadow clearly.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_weaver.idle: A broken thread can be tied. A melted needle is gone for good.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_weaver.meet: Look at this needle. Lightning came in through the window and melted only the loom's iron needle. Not a scorch on the cloth.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_weaver.meet2: My mother said the wind folk let lightning pass through copper. Six copper ingots, and a lightning rod for the roof. Then I can weave again.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_weaver.wait: Copper shows as green streaks, not deep in the hills. A lightning rod is three ingots stacked upright.
item.skyabyss.town.child_drawing.lore: A great wing in the sky. Beneath it, two children holding hands. One face is scribbled out.
lore.skyabyss.town.bell_echo.body:
I rang the bell atop the great tower, once.

The bell keeper says he heard a second toll. Late, and from the same height.

There was no one on the tower but me.
lore.skyabyss.town.bell_echo.title: The Echo of the Top Bell
lore.skyabyss.town.cellar_1.body:
The drunkard's tale, in the tavern cellar.

Beneath the sky there is another sky, at the bottom of the earth. The place where the four heartbeats go home, someday.

The sky below looks up at the sky above.
lore.skyabyss.town.cellar_1.title: The Sky Below
lore.skyabyss.town.cellar_2.body:
I put my ear to the far wall of the tavern cellar.

I heard wind. Wind drawn from above to below, down into the deep.

There is a passage behind the wall. The drunkard has the key.
lore.skyabyss.town.cellar_2.title: The Bricked-Up Wall
lore.skyabyss.town.cellar_3.body:
Deep in the tavern cellar, at the end of the passage behind the bricked-up wall, there is a sealed door.

Nothing is written on it. Only, at the height of the handle, the greasy mark of a hand.

The same size as mine.
lore.skyabyss.town.cellar_3.title: The Sealed Door
lore.skyabyss.town.grave_1.body:
I laid a flower on the nameless grave outside the west gate.

The gravekeeper said the flower left there each morning is the same colour as the one I picked. Same field, same flower.

I did not go to the graveyard this morning.
lore.skyabyss.town.grave_1.title: Flowers on the Nameless Grave
lore.skyabyss.town.grave_2.body:
When we washed the moss from the nameless grave, a single line appeared.

"Write it down before you forget."

The same hand as the first line in the camp notebook.
lore.skyabyss.town.grave_2.title: One Line Under the Moss
lore.skyabyss.town.grave_3.body:
The footprints from the nameless grave ended at the house of mourning on the south road.

A table set with one plate too many. Graveyard earth on the seat of the empty chair. One line traced in the ash on the table.

"Back again."

The finger that traced it was as wide as mine.
lore.skyabyss.town.grave_3.title: The Table in the House of Mourning
lore.skyabyss.town.grave_4.body:
I lit a candle before the nameless grave.

The gravekeeper said the coffin has always been empty. That it was dug by someone who meant to lie in it "one day".

The place for a name is still blank.
lore.skyabyss.town.grave_4.title: The Empty Coffin
lore.skyabyss.town.well_song.body:
Beneath the old well, at the end of a narrow way. On the wall, the same carvings as in the hall of songs.

The carving stops partway, as if the hand meant to finish it stopped there.

Held to my ear, the shard from the chest hummed the same song, far away.
lore.skyabyss.town.well_song.title: The Song at the Bottom of the Well
message.skyabyss.town.guide.none: Guide: Nothing left to add to your map, I'm afraid.
message.skyabyss.town.guide.rumor: Guide: "%1$s" lies %2$s of the capital, about %3$s blocks.
message.skyabyss.town.rumor.well: One of the grates on the old well to the southwest comes loose, they say. The children swear there's something down there.
message.skyabyss.town.well.found: In the chest at the bottom of the old well: bell coins, and a shard that hums faintly.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_1.done: Beneath the sky there is another sky. So the drunkard said.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_1.hand.hand: Give the honey pot to the drunkard
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_1.hand.journa: You have the honey. Give it to the drunkard.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_1.honey.journ: The drunkard in the cellar of the Deep Cup tavern wants something sweet. One honey pot.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_1.rumor: The drunk in the tavern cellar says he'll tell his best story for something sweet.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_1.summary: Give the drunkard a honey pot and hear his best story.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_1.title: Another Sky
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_2.back.journa: Behind the wall, wind was being drawn downward. Tell the drunkard.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_2.done: There's a passage behind the wall. Too early for the key.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_2.listen.jour: The drunkard says to put your ear against the far wall of the cellar.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_2.listen.list: Put your ear to the far cellar wall
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_2.rumor: The drunkard's been going on about the cellar's far wall making noises.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_2.summary: Put your ear to the far wall of the tavern cellar.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_2.title: Wind Behind the Wall
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_3.back.journa: You saw the sealed door. Tell the drunkard.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_3.done: Beyond the sealed door, they say, is the road to the sky below.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_3.open.journa: Three heartbeats returned. The drunkard says he'll open the far wall of the cellar.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_3.open.open: Have the drunkard open the wall
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_3.rumor: The drunkard said, dead sober, that it's time to hand over the key.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_3.summary: Open the cellar's far wall with the drunkard's key, and see the door at the end of the passage.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_3.title: The Old Key
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_3.walk.journa: The wall is open. Go see the door at the end of the passage. Don't try to open it.
quest.skyabyss.town.cellar_3.walk.walk: Walk to the end of the passage
quest.skyabyss.town.ch1_apprentice.clerk: Ask about the test at the Whale Chasers' Guild
The apprentice is afraid to sit the test alone. First, ask at the Whale Chasers' Guild desk what the test involves.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch1_apprentice.done: The apprentice's name is carved into the Whale Chasers' Guild's roll. The line beside it is still blank.
Give the bones to the apprentice
That's everything. Go back to the apprentice and hand over the bones.
Two tasks: drive off four night beasts, and bring back three bones. That's all you need on a titan's back, they say.
A rumour from the innkeeper: an apprentice due to sit the Whale Chasers' Guild's registration test lodges at the old soldier's house on the south road.
Meet the apprentice chaser (old soldier's house, south road)
quest.skyabyss.town.ch1_apprentice.rumor: An apprentice is lodging at the old soldier's house on the south road, about to sit the Whale Chasers' Guild's test. Says it's lonely going alone. Go say hello.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch1_apprentice.summa: Sit the Whale Chasers' Guild's registration test together with an apprentice.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch1_apprentice.title: The Apprentice Chaser
quest.skyabyss.town.ch1_bell.back.journa: It rang. Go down and tell the bell keeper.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch1_bell.done: The town counts its days again. The bell keeper never spoke of the second toll again.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch1_bell.meet.journa: A rumour from the innkeeper: the bell keeper wants someone to ring the top bell. He's at the scribe's house west of the square.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch1_bell.meet.meet: Meet the bell keeper (scribe's house, west of the square)
quest.skyabyss.town.ch1_bell.ring.journa: His knees can't take the tower stairs. The top bell hasn't rung since the night the shadow passed. Climb the tower and ring it once.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch1_bell.ring.ring: Ring the bell atop the great tower
quest.skyabyss.town.ch1_bell.rumor: The old bell keeper of the great tower is looking for young legs to ring the top bell. He rooms at the scribe's house west of the square.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch1_bell.summary: Ring the bell atop the great tower for the old bell keeper.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch1_bell.title: The Bell Keeper's Request
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_bard.back.back: Bring the verses to the bard
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_bard.back.journa: Three verses gathered. Take them to the bard.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_bard.done: The song goes on now: a song of the sea counting people.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_bard.listen.inn: Ask the innkeeper about the sea song
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_bard.listen.jour: The bard's song stops at "When the tide draws back, a road appears." The perch keeper, the innkeeper and the storage keeper may know more.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_bard.listen.perc: Ask the travel keeper at the perch about the sea song
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_bard.listen.stas: Ask the storage keeper about the sea song
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_bard.meet.journa: A rumour from the innkeeper: a bard is renting a house on the south avenue.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_bard.meet.meet: Meet the bard (lodgings on the south avenue)
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_bard.rumor: A bard has taken a house on the south avenue. He's hunting for the rest of a sea song, and wants to hear from the townsfolk.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_bard.summary: Gather the lost verses of a sea song from the people of the capital.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_bard.title: The Wandering Bard
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_net.back.journal: The spot is secured. Tell the fisher.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_net.done: For the first time in a long while, fish lie on the tide market's stalls.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_net.gather.journ: He dropped his net and ran the night the tide shell came ashore. He needs eight thread spools to mend it and three dried fish for the market.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_net.gather.strin: Gather thread to mend the net
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_net.hand.hand: Give the string and cod to the fisher
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_net.hand.journal: That's everything. Take it to the fisher.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_net.market.journ: The net is mended. The quickest way to a stall is to borrow the tool merchant's shopfront. The fisher isn't one for talking.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_net.market.marke: Ask the tool merchant for a market spot
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_net.meet.journal: A rumour from the innkeeper: a fisher who fled the shore is staying at the fisher's house on the east avenue.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_net.meet.meet: Meet the fisher (fisher's house, east avenue)
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_net.rumor: A fisher who abandoned the shore because of the tide shell has moved into a house on the east avenue. Wants to sell at the tide market, but his net is torn.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_net.summary: Mend the net of a fisher who fled the tide shell, so he can sell at the tide market.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_net.title: The Fisher's Net
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_sailor.done: The compass pointed north. The sailor marked the low-tide days on the map.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_sailor.hand.hand: Give the wayfinder and map to the sailor
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_sailor.hand.jour: That's everything. Give them to the sailor.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_sailor.make.jour: One wayfinder and one blank chart. Both are sold at the tool shop.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_sailor.meet.jour: A rumour from the innkeeper: the old sailor lost his compass to the tide. The sailor's house, northwest of the square.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_sailor.meet.meet: Meet the old sailor (the sailor's house)
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_sailor.rumor: The old sailor is grieving a compass the tide took. The sailor's house, northwest of the square.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_sailor.summary: Bring the old sailor a wayfinder and an empty map.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch2_sailor.title: The Sailor's Compass
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_lanterns.done: Three lanterns were lit. The children stopped counting the thunder and slept.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_lanterns.hand.ha: Give the lanterns to the mother
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_lanterns.hand.jo: That's three. Give them to the mother.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_lanterns.make.jo: Three lanterns. Sold at the tool shop.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_lanterns.meet.jo: A rumour from the innkeeper: the mother of a big family needs lights for stormy nights. A house on the south road.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_lanterns.meet.me: Meet the mother of the big family
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_lanterns.rumor: The mother of the big family needs lights for the storm nights. The house on the south road full of children's voices.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_lanterns.summary: Bring three lanterns to the mother of the big family.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_lanterns.title: Lanterns for a Stormy Night
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_thunder.done: The child fell asleep in a bed at the inn. She left a drawing behind.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_thunder.escort.i: Walk the child to the Bell Inn
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_thunder.escort.j: She was curled up on a bed no one uses. The inn has lights. Take her hand and walk her to the Bell Inn on the west avenue.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_thunder.find.fin: Find the child (house of mourning, south road)
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_thunder.find.jou: The youngest of the big family hid on a thunder night and hasn't come home. She was seen heading toward the house of mourning on the south road.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_thunder.inn.ask: Leave the child with the innkeeper
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_thunder.inn.jour: You've reached the inn. Ask the innkeeper to look after her.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_thunder.rumor: The youngest of the big family hides whenever thunder rolls. She did it last night and still hasn't turned up. ...Someone saw her heading toward the house of mourning on the south road.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_thunder.summary: Find the child who hid on a thunder night and never came home, and bring her to the inn.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_thunder.title: Thunder Night
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_weaver.done: The loom runs again. On thunder nights, they say, a wing pattern weaves itself in.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_weaver.gather.jo: The wind folk let lightning pass through copper, they say. Six copper lumps, and one lightning rod for the roof.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_weaver.hand.hand: Give the copper and lightning rod to the weaver
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_weaver.hand.jour: That's everything. Take it to the weaver.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_weaver.meet.jour: A rumour from the innkeeper: lightning melted a loom needle at the weaver's house on the west avenue.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_weaver.meet.meet: Meet the weaver (weaver's house, west avenue)
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_weaver.rumor: Lightning melted the needle in the weaver's loom, west avenue. She insists copper will let the lightning pass.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_weaver.summary: Bring copper and a lightning rod to replace the loom needle melted by lightning.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch3_weaver.title: The Weaver's Needle
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_ash.back.journal: The smith approved. Let the apprentice know.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_ash.done: A new forge burns in the smithy. Some say a thread of light runs down through its fire.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_ash.gather.journ: The master's forge can't melt ember ash. One blast furnace and four magma blocks for the bed. The material trader stocks both.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_ash.hand.hand: Give the blast furnace and magma to the apprentice
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_ash.hand.journal: That's everything. Take it to the apprentice.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_ash.meet.journal: A rumour from the innkeeper: the smith's apprentice wants a new forge for the ember mountain's ash. He's at the apprentices' lodging on the south road.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_ash.meet.meet: Meet the smith's apprentice (apprentices' lodging, south road)
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_ash.rumor: The smith's apprentice hauled ash back from the southern mountain. He's fired up about building a new forge.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_ash.smith.journa: The forge is built. The apprentice is afraid to tell his master. Tell the smith yourself.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_ash.smith.smith: Tell the smith about the new forge
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_ash.summary: Help the smith's apprentice build a new forge that can melt the ash of the ember mountain.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_ash.title: The Ash Apprentice
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_baker.done: The oven fire held. The ash-baked bread stayed a little warm and never quite cooled.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_baker.gather.jou: Sixteen wheat sheaves and four charcoal.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_baker.hand.hand: Give the wheat sheaves and charcoal to the baker
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_baker.hand.journ: That's everything. Give it to the baker.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_baker.meet.journ: A rumour from the innkeeper: the baker's oven fire is failing. The baker's house on the northeast road.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_baker.rumor: The baker's oven has been weak since the ash began to fall. The house on the northeast road that smells so good.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_baker.summary: Bring the baker wheat sheaves and charcoal to keep the oven burning.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_baker.title: Ash-Baked Bread
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_herbs.brew.journ: Bring two potions. Sold at the apothecary.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_herbs.done: You brought the potions. Only the ash, she said, must never go in.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_herbs.hand.hand: Show the potions to the herbalist
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_herbs.hand.journ: That's two. Show them to the herbalist.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_herbs.meet.journ: A rumour from the innkeeper: the old herbalist wants to see a potion someone brewed. She lives in the herb house on the south road.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_herbs.meet.meet: Meet the old herbalist (herb house, south road)
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_herbs.rumor: The old herb gatherer wants to see some potions. The apothecary has plenty.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_herbs.summary: Bring two potions to the old herb gatherer. Potions are sold at the apothecary.
quest.skyabyss.town.ch4_herbs.title: The Herbalist's Pot
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_1.done: The words were not a name.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_1.flower.journ: The nameless grave outside the west gate. Someone leaves a flower there every morning. Pick a flower and bring it to the gravekeeper.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_1.lay.journal: You have a flower. Give it to the gravekeeper and lay it together.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_1.lay.lay: Give the flower to the gravekeeper
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_1.rumor: The gravekeeper wants help with the nameless grave. His hut is outside the west gate.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_1.summary: Lay a flower on the nameless grave, then wash the moss from the stone and read what lies beneath.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_1.title: The Nameless Grave
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_3.back.journal: Earth on the empty chair in the house of mourning. One line traced in the ash on the table. Tell the gravekeeper.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_3.done: The grave was dug for someone who would "one day" lie in it. The rest lies further on.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_3.rumor: The gravekeeper is troubled again. Someone tried to dig up the nameless grave in the night.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_3.summary: Follow the footprints of whoever tried to dig up the nameless grave, then light a candle before it.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_3.title: Turned Earth
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_3.visit.journa: Someone tried to dig up the nameless grave in the night. The footprints lead into the capital, toward the house of mourning on the south road.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_3.visit.visit: Follow the footprints (house of mourning, south road)
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_tbc: The gravekeeper's tale continues in chapter six.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_inner_ferryman.a:
Crossing to the other land? When it is calm, it is no time at all.
Climb in.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_inner_ferryman.s:
This sea is warm. Now and then something deep down turns over in its sleep.
...The tide folk say the shelled one slept here once.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_1.wash.journal: You have the water. Bring it to the gravekeeper.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_1.wash.wash: Give the water to the gravekeeper
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_1.water.journa: There are letters under the moss on the nameless grave. Fill a bucket with water and bring it to the gravekeeper.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_3.candle.journ: Bring the gravekeeper a candle to light before the nameless grave.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_3.light.journa: You have a candle. Give it to the gravekeeper.
quest.skyabyss.town.grave_3.light.light: Give the candle to the gravekeeper
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_town_guide_whale:
Welcome to Whalewatch. When the lookout bell rings, look up.
Looking for a shop? Tell me where, and I'll light the way at your feet.
Show me to a shop (lit path)
Welcome to Tidekeep. Everyone gets lost in the salt smell once.
Looking for a shop? Tell me where, and I'll light the way.
Show me to a shop (lit path)
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_town_guide_storm:
You climbed all the way to Windwait. Don't let the wind push you off the street.
Looking for a shop? Tell me where, and I'll light the way.
Show me to a shop (lit path)
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_town_guide_ember:
Welcome to Ashforge. The ash makes it hard to see your feet.
Looking for a shop? Tell me where, and I'll light the way.
Show me to a shop (lit path)
dialogue.skyabyss.attendant_guide.menu.t: Rumors of places I haven't been
dialogue.skyabyss.attendant_guide.town_r: I hear plenty from travelers at the gates. Let me tell you of places not yet on your map.
dialogue.skyabyss.attendant_guide.town_d: I know the bearing and the road to the ruins from the capital. I'll mark one on your map.
quest.skyabyss.town.rumor_bone_pit.title: Sounds in the Pit
quest.skyabyss.town.rumor_bone_pit.summa: A rumour from the Kujirami guide: something lives at the bottom of the Whalebone Pit. Go and see.
quest.skyabyss.town.rumor_bone_pit.done: A centipede was digging through the titan's bones. The guide will tell the miners they can stop digging.
quest.skyabyss.town.rumor_bone_pit.go.jo: East of town, a rock mouth leads down to the old pit where titan bone was dug. Miners fled from a huge bone-eating centipede.
quest.skyabyss.town.rumor_bone_pit.clear: The master at the very bottom. Suggested Lv 10.
Defeat the master of the Whalebone Pit
The master is down. Tell the guide.
dialogue.skyabyss.guest_town_guide_whale: Report the master of the Whalebone Pit

Do you know the rock mouth on the hill east of town? It's the old pit where they dug titan bone.
Lately a miner came running out, saying a huge centipede was eating the bones down there. If you could look, the town would rest easier.

You beat the centipede? ...Thank you. I'll tell the miners.
